item.title: SCP - The God Killer
item.description: An extra dimenstional SCP that was betrayed by its people then cast out of its universe after killing all the gods from its dimension.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Small bit of Horror, Drama/Emotional, bit of Action, some History

Page Layout (Optional): Standard Description and Containment Procedures, interview, discovery log, and requests.

Elevator Pitch: it is basically a man that can change his size to anything he wants, is completely invincable and unstoppable. (except for the gases that the foundation make) he was originally made to kill gods and devour them. shredding them down to their atoms. but he gets betrayed by the humans and sent to the SCP universe.

Central Narrative: the basic idea of this, is that the SCP is from another universe. in that universe gods exist (like Odin and Zeus) each one basically owning a portion of the world and making it their own. but after millions of years of the gods and other smaller deities ruling the world. the humans become fed up. the combine magic and science to create SCP-XXXX (no number) this entity is made to destroy the gods one by one and free man kind. but little do they know that with every god, deity and demi-god it kills it gains a little bit of humanity. eventually after killing and devouring every last god, he has become essetially human. but when e returns and is told the kill code, he lives and realises that they tried to kill him after all he did for them. he begins to attack the humans, but they open a wormhole and he is sent to the scp universe, where he gets contained and evetually stored.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: whats special about this idea is that we get to see the building of a god from another world. and after he learns about being human he instantly doesn't want to be one because of what his people did to him. so it's like a betrayal story that makes people feel empathy for him, then sadness as he gets betrayed again in the SCP universe.

Additional Notes: i would love this idea to reach draft status, as i have had this idea for a novel for a long time and i thought it would be great to get feedback from here. and if it became and scp. it would make a great story character to have in many different stories.
anyway im blabbering too much and i really thank you for reading my idea! :)

item.title: Modern Day Soldier
item.description: has exceptional skills in hand-to-hand combat and use of modern day weaponry
item.content:encoded:
First SCP idea. An entity that takes the form of a soldier. This soldier has exceptional skills in hand-to-hand combat and use of modern day weaponry.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlight: Yes!

Page Type: SCP Article.

Elevator Pitch: My SCP idea is an entity that takes a form of a soldier (pretty much a U.S Soldier).

  • Has a unique form that make him invulnerable to most damage (mainly being bullets, his form weakens by any sort of explosives)
  • Has weapons that are connected to him and cannot be removed (if someone attempts to, the soldier gets irritated and even aggressive)
  • The soldier entity gets PTSD an effect that resembles PTSD, while in this state, he goes berserk, destroying everything he sees in a fit of rage.
  • Can communicate with humans in mainly English
+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: This SCP is an unknown entity that takes the form of a soldier. No one knows exactly what the entity is or why it's taking the form of a soldier, but theories are that the entity was released from an unknown containment in an anonymous operation led by the U.S Government. This SCP is an excellent hand-to-hand fighter, shooter, and uses military strategies. This SCP is also known to be relatively peaceful (as it is a soldier), but can be violent if angered, or in the state of his PTSD effect. The U.S Government insists that they know nothing of the soldier, but some scientists think they are lying. SCP officials think that the soldier was once a leader of the squad with how he talks and uses his strategies of moving through buildings/locations and how secretive he is in interviews. The form of this SCP is unknown to SCP officials as it's an unusual substance and can make the wearer immune to most damage. This SCP is known to get out of containment easily when angered by officials or D-Class, but seems blind when in it's PTSD effect.

Hook/Attention-Grabbers: I find this idea for an SCP to be unique because you don't see a lot of humanoid SCPs with actual guns. I find that what's best about SCPs is the mystery around them; like where they come from and what the goals of the SCPs are. This idea has a bit of mystery of who the soldier is, what the form substance could be, and I will probably add more mysteries to this SCP if I am able to write about it.

The overall concepts that I think makes this idea unique: An SCP who uses modern day weapons to dispatch enemies, the mystery of this SCP, and that it's a soldier SCP.

Additional Notes: NONE.

item.title: Your Friendly Neighbourhood Thermonuclear Bomb
item.description: AKA, why you should learn to stop worrying and love store-brand potato salad.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Elevator Pitch: A cardboard standee for a nuclear bomb informational evening come to life. Displays all signs of an activated thermonuclear weapon. 1950's-60's sociable. Invites people to dinner to inform them of the benefits of thermonuclear weapons.

Central Narrative: "The Bomb" is sapient and sentient cardboard cutout of a thermonuclear missile, with limbs attached via twist-pins. Despite being made of cardboard and rudimentary electronics causing it's actuation, it displays the exact same properties as a live thermonuclear bomb. It's purpose is to talk to and convince it's "neighbors" (read: any sapient/sentient object nearby) of the many uses and benefits of thermonuclear weaponry. Has a very 1950's-60's "idyllic" nuclear home outlook. Will try to invite it's "neighbors" over for barbecue dinners, where, nearing the end of the dinner, continuing it's idealization of thermonuclear weapons. it will produce potato salad wherein the potatoes have been baked via thermonuclear detonation (edible, but probably not healthy). Found near Nye County, Nevada, reports it was "clear to be activated" when a disgruntled nuclear information evening worker dumped potato salad on the electronics causing it to move and speak.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Creepy insistence on the benefit of thermonuclear weaponry to an almost absurd degree. 1950's-60's delusion. Potato salad.

Additional Notes: Please do not attempt to ride the cardboard cut-out with a cowboy hat. We tried, and it did not appreciate it.

item.title: SCP Snow Globe Idea Seeking Greenlight
item.description: An anomalous snow globe that contains the beginnings of a human society.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: An anomalous snow globe that contains a fully functional society of individuals who have been transported into it. The victims of the globe are almost instantaneously erased from all historical records and human memory.

Central Narrative: In December, 2019, a low level foundation member purchased a snow globe from a Christmas shop to gift his significant other. It caught his eye because of the realistic landscape of the snow globe, but when the gift was opened a half a month later, there were certain features that had appeared on the landscape that the foundation member were not there when he purchased the globe, such as a crop field and a few crude houses. The foundation personnel brought the globe to the foundation and has since been on 24-hour observation by a camera which has documented the progress of the internal civilization.

+ show block
– hide block

While on an expedition/hunting an SCP/recovering from a containment breach, a foundation team reported the immediate disappearance of a team member, as if he had been swallowed up by the air in front of him. As foundation command began to question the team on the specifics of the disappearance immediately following the incident, they could not recall the existence of the team member at all, and foundation records of the team suggested likewise. The identification of a disappearance was nonetheless recorded. The anomalous properties of the snow globe were only discovered when the camera observing the snow globe recorded a flare gun fire from within the forest of the globe approximately 3 minutes after the disappearance of the team member. Currently no attempts have been made from the inhabitants of the interior to communicate with the foundation, and it is unknown whether the victims are aware of their situation. When foundation personnel revisited the site of the disappearance, nothing occurred, and the source of victimization remains unknown.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: While the idea of a miniature self-contained civilization isn’t completely unique, the events that resulted in the discovery of the anomaly is testament to the aptitude of the foundation. Someone had to be curious enough, or the foundation is thorough enough, that the cross reference between the report of the disappearance and the observation of the flare within the globe was able to occur. Regardless, it was a fun and engaging idea to develop.

Additional Notes: I’m open to ideas on making the civilization itself more engaging, but I think the disconnect between the inhabitants of the globe and the foundation is interesting on its own. I’m also considering including a label that says SCP Foundation, which would allude that the globe might be a failed experiment and/or one from another reality.

item.title: Ideas for execution of a "Monster What Kills You" skip
item.description: I like a challenge.
item.content:encoded:
At some point in the near future (perhaps after the posting of one or more other articles) I would really like to take on the writing challenge of making a "classic monster" skip interesting. It's such a commonly-avoided topic that I can't help but be enticed to try and make it work. Here are some qualities such a hypothetical monster would have to include, as part of the challenge:

  • Very little in the way of motivation, i.e. a predator or something similar
  • Irrepressibly violent tendencies towards humans, i.e. this is just a thing what kills you
  • No cop-outs or deceptions as to its nature, i.e. it is exactly what it seems to be.

Given these constraints, the most plausible avenue to success seems to be setting the monster within a narrative that stands on its own. However, even that feels like cheating to me, as by shifting the focus of the article from the monster to the story, I've effectively conceded that it is simply impossible to make a monster interesting nowadays.

Does anyone know of some modern skips that could provide inspiration? Do you have any ideas about what would be necessary to make this challenge possible? Do you believe it is possible at all? Should I abort this ill-conceived venture at once??? Please let me know.

If it goes well, I might try to do the same for an x-man.

item.title: A Faucet with its Drop.
item.description: A pretty simple SCP, but as it is docile, is also beyond dangerous.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article (with ACS)

Genre(Optional):Unsure

Page Layout(Optional): Standard, along with certain features including an O5-only document secured with a SCiPNet Login.

Elevator Pitch:

SCP-XXXX has an appearance that of a faucet from manufacturer "Delta Faucets". SCP-XXXX can function similarly to a usual faucet, with the exception that the water by SCP-XXXX usually has a discharge rate of 61.6 μL/s, whether supplied with water or not. If so that SCP-XXXX is not supplied with water, the drops will be more purplish per 17 minutes of use. SCP-XXXX is sentient this is confirmed as SCP-XXXX can communicate in Morse, discovered after a level 4 researcher, who was fluent in Morse, noticed that the drops discharged by SCP-XXXX took in the order of
…. .. / .- (- -.) (.-) (..) (-.) (- -..- -) / -.. .-. .-.-.-, to which translate to "hi again, dr.".

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX can also create music with its drops, as such to the range from note C1 to F7. Led to an incident of it playing SCP-407.

A simpler description of this would be the fact that SCP-XXXX separates the waveform of the human voice when entered upon an oscillator. Pitches made by SCP-XXXX, when combined, make a waveform that someone would identify as a recording of someone's voice seemingly in his 40's, talking to someone he calls "Aleph". When questioned about who "Aleph" is, SCP-XXXX stated that "Aleph" was actually the level 4 researcher. Said researcher was notified of this recording and proceeded to interview SCP-XXXX for further questioning.

SCP-XXXX once distributed information kept hidden by the O5, how it knew that information is currently unknown.

Central Narrative:
The article has interviews with SCP-XXXX, some in Morse Code, and a visualized explanation of the exceedingly complex form of communication used by SCP-XXXX. Will be in ACS, classified safe,
disruption class Vlam (due to the SCP-407 incident), Risk class Critical (also of SCP-407).

Hook/Attention Grabber:
As much as it is sentient, SCP-XXXX shows a fair degree of omniscience. Morse code known by SCP-XXXX is international, but also fluent in American Morse. The extremely complex communication is basically:

  • Get some waves
  • Translate it to drops
  • Get those waves and combine them
  • Get an oscillator and combine them
  • Play the combined wave

SCP-XXXX has no recollection of how it knows O5 information.

Additional Notes:
I actually got this idea while in the shower. I stood just in front of the faucet and was mesmerized by how the drops falling resembled music. It gave me an idea, however.

He also has a rhyme that can be used to summon him at any time, but it is in constant flux. The rhyme constantly changes the way it goes and and where it shows up. It will randomly select towns in the entire world and when it chooses one, everyone in the town will think they always knew the rhyme existed, but the previous town will completely forget the rhyme was even real.

When summoned, this SCP will hunt down the summoner/summoners and kill them in a variety of ways. He is also able to extend his limbs an infinite length.

His body is so black, it absorbs light to the point that he looks just like a shadow taken three dimensions.

Despite being immortal and being able to be summoned at any point in time, he really hates it. All he wants is to be left alone and not summoned at all. But he has no control over the rhyme.

item.title: ONE YEAR/REMEMBER DEATH
item.description: Mind-affecting SCP /cognitohazard/Memetic Hazard/Keter/Neutralized
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: The anomaly was a former channel on the media site “YouTube” that was active from 11/15/19 to 11/15/20 exactly one year from its creation.

The channel uploaded what would seem like fun original content but was littered with cognitohazardous material that has now been completely neutralized. Two humanoids are present in every video and host the channel. Both entities are almost identical to two other famous people but are not the same people.

Subjects who view any of the 365 videos are instantly met with a clock that counts down starting from 365:00:00. The anomaly’s effects immediate initiate at the start of every video by infecting and manipulating the subject’s mind making them perceive the two entities as gods and begin to worship the two entities in nonsensical and sometimes violent ways. Afflicted subjects attempt to spread the anomaly through social media and other chat related applications.

The anomaly can not be deleted directly by YouTube since attempts to do so crash all electronic devices.

The two entities seen in every video seem to not be a part of our dimension but from another reality. Since they cannot be located and have been seen with anomalous items that do cannot exist in our reality.
Central Narrative: The Narrative would dictate all of the foundations attempts to neutralize the anomaly and work with YouTube to contain the anomaly from spreading. Millions of viewers have already been infected by the anomaly and spread of the anomaly drastically increases. The Foundation worries that an AK end of the world scenario could occur as tens of millions of people rapidly fall under the anomaly’s influence. As governments collapse and people perform violent rituals in the streets the channel finally reaches its climatic end

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Based on a real experiment conducted on the same website.

Additional Notes: The central narrative would begin by detailing the small amount of infection but slowly starts getting worse and worse until the end. Not all details described here it would be too long.

item.title: Inaccurate Extradimensional War Reenactment
item.description: Extradimensional beings who like to reenact human wars
item.content:encoded:
Extradimensional beings who like to reenact human wars, but have a few of the details wrong.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Comedy

Elevator Pitch: A phenomenon that manifests near the locations and annual anniversaries of famous battles. Terrain and weather in the affected area reconfigure to match the original battle, and invisible and intangible entities manifest to reenact it, along with the appropriate military hardware, which is visible but still intangible. The Foundation initially thinks that these entities are ghosts, but they eventually notice that they’re sentient and aware of their surroundings, then attempts to make contact. The Foundation briefly speaks with the entities, enough to realize some humorous misconceptions the entities have about how human war works in three-dimensional space. Eventually, the entities manifest to reenact a battle that never happened. When the Foundation points this out, the entities realize they’re in the wrong universe and demanifest, never to return.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The Foundation first discovers this phenomenon when it manifests near a populated area. There’s a log of notable manifestations (current list includes the Battles of Bull Run/Manassas, Hastings, Rorke’s Drift, and Megiddo, plus a prehistoric conflict between Homo sapiens and Neanderthals and a battle between the Mongols and Daevites). The log notes illustrate the Foundation’s dawning awareness of the entities’ sentience and attempts to interact, concluding with a final log of a manifestation somewhere in the Southern US that doesn’t correspond with any known battle. There are two addenda after that: one chronicling a humorous interaction between a Foundation personnel and one of the entities and one chronicling the final encounter with the anomaly, during which they realize they’re in the wrong place (“We’re in the wrong universe, you stupid idiot!”).

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The bait-and-switch of anomalies that seem to be ghosts but are actually slightly confused extradimensional war-reenacters is an amusing twist. I also intend to imply or even crosslink that the nonexistent battle is the one described by SCP-592. I plan to eventually write a Tale about the universe full of faceless people described by that book and encountered in SCP-970.

Additional Notes: I’m not sure if I should have the anomalies manifest at the actual locations of the battles or on some shapeshifting island or something out in the middle of nowhere. Having them at the actual locations requires all sorts of memetic/amnestic foolery on the part of the Foundation and/or the entities to preserve normalcy, which I worry would bloat the Description and stretch suspension of disbelief.

item.title: The Tainted Saint Collection (Seeking Greenlight)
item.description: Parasitic donor organs
item.content:encoded:
Parasitic donor organs that, following surgical implantation, rot and digest their hosts.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror

Page Layout: Standard

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a Euclid-class collection of parasitic donor organs that are capable of osmotic extracellular digestion. Individual "fragments" of SCP-XXXX possess passive, non-lethal cognitohazardous properties.

Central Narrative: The Tainted Saint Collection is the first entry in a wider narrative I have planned. It's centered around the research of Dr. Lee Elliot, an ex-field agent with an interest in SCPs that can manipulate organic matter. I intend for this narrative to begin (temporally) with a different SCP, an incident report, and a Tale. However, this SCP seemed like a better place to start in practice since it's easier to pitch.

+ show block
– hide block

The report starts out normal, with little off-kilter details sprinkled in to breed unease. Note, I described SCP-XXXX as a collection of donor organs in the intro here, but in the article itself that information will not be revealed until the description section. By the time the reader reaches that point, I want them to be hyperaware of the danger associated with even brief contact so the reveal that they were implanted into people hits as hard as possible.

Beyond that, the bulk of the article's narrative will follow the background of each fragment individually, outlining their quirks. SCP-XXXX-B, for example, kills its hosts within a few days, whereas SCP-XXXX-A remained inside the same host for six months. At the end, I plan on including a brief interview between SCP-XXXX-A's ex-host and Dr. Elliot. Lastly, I'll include a short lab report detailing a non-lethal vivisection of SCP-XXXX-A that ended up costing Dr. Elliot his left eye. Spoiler alert: fragments of SCP-XXXX are immobile by choice, not biology.

Hook/Attention Grabber: They're carnivorous donor organs with cognitohazardous properties. I know I'd read an article about that.

Additional Notes: I have way too much experience writing formal academic prose, so my main concern is getting the lore/terminology right. I'm also wondering if anyone knows some good SCPs that introduce recurring researcher characters without making that introduction too intrusive. I don't want the article to end up feeling like it's about Dr. Elliot.

item.title: Medicine Man - first scp idea
item.description: My first scp idea (seeking greenlight). About a sculpture that invades one's consciousness
item.content:encoded:
My first scp idea (seeking greenlight). About a sculpture that invades one's consciousness when activated. This new consciousness has a vast knowledge of chemistry and biology.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

  • The Medicine Man is a sculpture that activates when an individual lowers their guard or gets distracted within the statue's area of effect. The victim is unaware of this, but will see the manifestation of the sculpture's consciousness (as in "its soul"), which calls itself The Medicine Man. Once confronted with the medicine man, said individual will never be able to fully focus/concentrate again (unknowingly), which makes the individual more vulnerable to the sculpture's effect. When exposed to the statue for too long, one could enter a comatose state or develop Alzheimer's.
+ show block
– hide block
  • When trying to prevent an individual from totally succumbing to the medicine man by attempting to improve their ability to focus with external forces (caffeine, adrenaline injection, etc.), Medicine Man will switch said individual's consciousness with itself, trapping the individual consciousness in the statue. Medicine Man can then host a body until it finds another statue to reside in.

item.description: Seems like the little buggers can get into anything...
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Not yet, I suppose…?

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Sci-Fi, Nature Documentary, Comedy(?)

Elevator Pitch: Termites with a nest-building behavior that can bypass conventional spatial limitations, including covering immense distances and moving in and out of perfectly sealed spaces. Pretty much the same goals, needs, and individual intelligence of ordinary termites in all other respects.

Central Narrative: The first clue is the identification of Australian compass termites somewhere that they definitely should not be. Further investigation leads to exploration of their tunnels and the discovery that distant places are connected through seemingly-random twists and turns, which the insects have no trouble navigating but are confusing to a human sense of direction. There's a conspicuous lack of pocket dimensions, thaumaturgical Ways, or significant gravitational anomalies involved, at least as far as the Foundation can initially detect.

The Foundation would be up against mundane technological limitations on what sort of equipment can fit down an individual termite tunnel, as any substantial damage to the structures promptly collapses their anomalous effects.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: We have an otherwise mostly mundane (if highly industrious) social insect species that cannot be reliably confined to a single habitat, although it's not an immediate Veil risk unless people start trying to identify individual termite species. What's more, they've created a functional hyperspace network out of nothing but soil and their own feces - and wouldn't the Foundation just love to learn how that works?

Additional Notes: Researching mundane eusocial insects is still relatively cutting-edge science, since they tend to live underground and it's hard to study large-scale emergent behaviors outside their natural habitat. I intend to research more into the kinds of technology used for these purposes, and play with how the Foundation might take them further. I could see this having a lot of experiment logs - perhaps taking reader suggestions, if the article were to take off.

item.title: The Indigo Branch (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Mystery

Elevator Pitch: A dark web page that lists the names of many different people, ranked from 1 to 100. Each name is accompanied by a price, and the names change almost daily. Anyone who views the site will always end up on the list and disappear sometime in the future.

Central Narrative: A recent suicide in urban California has a man dead at his computer, a note at his side, and a bullet through his head. The paper talks of the Indigo Branch, and how to get to it on the dark web. It also talks about how the man had received a steady amount of cryptocurrency over the past few months, and with his life in a bad situation, began using the money in an effort to turn everything around. The sender quickly begins talking to him, and says they will continue giving him money as long as he uses his coding knowledge to help locate information on the people whose names appear on the site. He soon stops helping the anonymous sender, and finds his name in the seventh spot on the list within a few days. He decided to kill himself rather than face the online criminals for his mistake.

+ show block
– hide block

An interested Foundation personnel looks deeper into this case, and starts using the site to track down the people he sees high up on the list. He finds that they all disappear at seemingly random times, some only hours after being on the list, and others who never disappeared before the personnel went missing himself. Because of the bizarre way these people go missing - seeming to vanish out of thin air most times - the Indigo Branch was categorized as an anomaly, and is only viewable by those with higher clearance.

Hook/Attention Grabber: Instead of another entity that just rips your face off for looking at it, or a spooky room that turns you into a chair, the Indigo Branch is just a single web page with names and numbers, who change at random intervals and correspond to real people. Less than being horrifying, this SCP is mysterious, allowing the reader to interpret everything in their own way.

Additional Notes: My biggest concern here is if I mistakenly wrote something that has already been written and solidified as an SCP. There are so many out there, and I have only read a few here and there, that is is a distinct possibility it may already exist. If this is the case, please let me know!
